summary: Part O0 of the blueprint for overconvergent Hilbert modular forms. This first checkpoint plans the Hilbert weights of BHW §6.1 at the level of points: 𝒪_p = ℤ_p ⊗ 𝒪_F with its norm and principal units, the geometric weights (characters of 𝒪_p^×) and arithmetic weights (characters of 𝒪_p^× × ℤ_p^×), the weight map ρ(w, t) = w²·(t^{-1} ∘ N) with its dual group map x ↦ (x², N(x)^{-1}), BHW's identity (9.1) on totally positive units, a radius parameter |T_κ| taken over a pro-p subgroup, boundedness of continuous characters into uniform Banach algebras, and analytic continuation of bounded weights (BHW Proposition 6.3). Two mistakes of BHW are recorded: the printed group map defining ρ lacks the inversion that its displayed formula has, and |T_κ| as printed is 1 for every weight nontrivial on the prime-to-p torsion, which falsifies the stated boundedness criterion and forces ε_κ = 0. Stages O1–O7 are not yet read.

nodes.title: Units at p of a number field
nodes.statement: For a number field F and a prime p, 𝒪_p := ℤ_p ⊗_ℤ 𝒪_F with its ℤ_p-algebra structure from the left factor and the ℤ_p-module topology. It is a finite free ℤ_p-module of rank [F : ℚ], a compact topological ring, and T(ℤ_p) := 𝒪_p^× (with the units topology) is BHW's T(ℤ_p) for T = Res_{𝒪_F|ℤ} G_m.
hypotheses: No hypothesis on how p decomposes in F: 𝒪_p is the product of the completed local rings at the primes above p, not assumed unramified or split.
Scalars on the left, so that the pinned base-change instances apply.
proofSteps: Define Op F p := ℤ_[p] ⊗[ℤ] 𝓞 F; its ℤ_p-algebra structure is Algebra.TensorProduct.leftAlgebra.
Module.Finite from Module.Finite.base_change and Module.Free from Module.Free.tensor, since 𝓞 F is finite free over ℤ.
Give it moduleTopology ℤ_[p] (an IsModuleTopology instance); it is a topological ring by IsModuleTopology.isTopologicalRing.

Rank: Module.finrank_baseChange with NumberField.RingOfIntegers.rank. Compactness: a ℤ_p-basis identifies 𝒪_p with ℤ_p^n by a linear equivalence, which is a homeomorphism for module topologies (IsModuleTopology.continuous_of_linearMap), and ℤ_p is compact (PadicInt.compactSpace).
acceptance: F = ℚ: 𝒪_p ≅ ℤ_p as ℤ_p-algebras, via Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv.
The topology is not discrete; a definition by the discrete topology would make every character continuous and the weight space far too large.
F = ℚ(i), p = 5: 𝒪_p ≅ ℤ_5 × ℤ_5, and T(ℤ_5) = (ℤ_5^×)², matching Res_{𝒪_F|ℤ} G_m at a split prime.

uses.how: the torus T(ℤ_p) = 𝒪_p^× whose characters are the geometric weights, and 𝒪_p ⊂ Res_{𝒪_F|ℤ} P^1 on which the Hodge–Tate period map lands.

sources.match: T(ℤ_p) = (𝒪_F ⊗ ℤ_p)^× is the group whose characters form the weight spaces.

nodes.title: The norm on units at p
nodes.statement: N : 𝒪_p^× → ℤ_p^× is the norm Algebra.norm ℤ_p (the determinant of multiplication on the free ℤ_p-module 𝒪_p), restricted to units. It is a continuous homomorphism, and N(1 ⊗ a) = N_{F/ℚ}(a) for a ∈ 𝒪_F.
proofSteps: Units.map of the monoid hom Algebra.norm ℤ_[p] : 𝒪_p →* ℤ_p.
Continuity: in a ℤ_p-basis the norm is a polynomial in the coordinates (Algebra.norm_apply, LinearMap.det), and coordinates are continuous for the module topology.
Compatibility: multiplication by 1 ⊗ a is the base change of multiplication by a on 𝒪_F, so its determinant is N_{F/ℚ}(a) (LinearMap.det_baseChange).
acceptance: F = ℚ: N is the identity of ℤ_p^×.
N(1 ⊗ η) = 1 for a totally positive unit η of a totally real F (used by weight-comparison-totally-positive-units).

nodes.title: Principal units 1 + p^r 𝒪_p
nodes.statement: For r ≥ 0, H_r := {x ∈ 𝒪_p^× : x − 1 ∈ p^r 𝒪_p} is an open subgroup of finite index of 𝒪_p^×; for r ≥ 1 it is a pro-p group, so it meets the prime-to-p torsion of 𝒪_p^× trivially.
proofSteps: Closure under products and inverses: (1 + p^r a)(1 + p^r b) = 1 + p^r(a + b + p^r ab), and the inverse of a unit ≡ 1 mod p^r is ≡ 1 mod p^r.
Openness: p^r 𝒪_p is open in the module topology (a finite-index ℤ_p-submodule), and H_r is its translate intersected with the open units.
Finite index: 𝒪_p^×/H_r injects into (𝒪_p/p^r)^×, a finite group.
Pro-p for r ≥ 1: H_r/H_s is a p-group for s ≥ r, being filtered by the additive groups p^i 𝒪_p/p^{i+1} 𝒪_p.
acceptance: r = 0 gives all of 𝒪_p^×.
F = ℚ, p odd, r = 1: H_1 = 1 + pℤ_p, of index p − 1; a nontrivial (p−1)-st root of unity is not in H_1.
This is the subgroup over which the corrected |T_κ| is taken (source issue E2).

uses.how: the pro-p subgroup over which |T_κ| is taken.

nodes.title: Geometric Hilbert weights
nodes.statement: For a topological commutative ring R, the R-points of the weight space 𝒲* for G* are the continuous characters T(ℤ_p) = 𝒪_p^× → R^×: GeomWeight F p R := ContinuousMonoidHom 𝒪_p^× R^×. BHW's 𝒲* = Spf(ℤ_p⟦T(ℤ_p)⟧)^an_η × L is the rigid space representing this functor on affinoid L-algebras; its construction and representability are requested from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L0a.
hypotheses: R a topological commutative ring, R^× with the units topology.
No analyticity or algebraicity is assumed: an arbitrary continuous character is a weight, not an algebraic weight.
proofSteps: Definition: ContinuousMonoidHom (Op F p)ˣ Rˣ. It is a commutative group under pointwise multiplication, and post-composition with continuous ring maps R → R' makes it a functor.
acceptance: F = ℚ: GeomWeight ℚ p R is the set of continuous characters ℤ_p^× → R^×, BHW's weight space for GL_2/ℚ (Definition 3.1).
Algebraic weights x ↦ N(x)^k (k ∈ ℤ) and x ↦ ∏_σ σ(x)^{k_σ} (after extending scalars to split F) are weights; a finite-order character of 𝒪_p^× is a weight that is not algebraic.
Continuity matters: a discontinuous homomorphism 𝒪_p^× → ℚ_p^× (which exists by choice on a ℚ-basis of the torsion-free part) is not a weight.

uses.how: sheaves ω^κ of overconvergent Hilbert modular forms for G* of weight κ.
the coefficient character of the equivariant sheaf.

nodes.title: Arithmetic Hilbert weights
nodes.statement: For a topological commutative ring R, the R-points of the weight space 𝒲 for G are the continuous characters of T(ℤ_p) × ℤ_p^×: ArithWeight F p R := ContinuousMonoidHom (𝒪_p^× × ℤ_p^×) R^×. Every such character is uniquely a pair (w, t) with w ∈ GeomWeight and t : ℤ_p^× → R^× continuous, via κ(x, y) = w(x)t(y).
proofSteps: Definition: ContinuousMonoidHom ((Op F p)ˣ × ℤ_[p]ˣ) Rˣ. ArithWeight.mk w t := (w ∘ fst)·(t ∘ snd) (ContinuousMonoidHom.fst, ContinuousMonoidHom.snd, pointwise product).
Bijectivity of (w, t) ↦ ArithWeight.mk w t: restrict κ to 𝒪_p^× × 1 and 1 × ℤ_p^×; a character of a product of groups is the product of its restrictions.
acceptance: F = ℚ: pairs of characters of ℤ_p^×.
(w, t) = (1, 1) gives the trivial weight.
The decomposition is unique: ArithWeight.mk is injective.

nodes.title: The group map dual to the weight map
nodes.statement: ι : 𝒪_p^× → 𝒪_p^× × ℤ_p^×, x ↦ (x², N(x)^{-1}), a continuous group homomorphism. It is the map for which pulling back characters gives BHW's displayed formula κ = w²·(t^{-1} ∘ N); BHW print x ↦ (x², N(x)) (source issue E1).
hypotheses: The inversion on the second coordinate is deliberate: it is what the displayed formula and BHW (9.1) require.
proofSteps: ι is a homomorphism because 𝒪_p^× and ℤ_p^× are commutative: (xy)² = x²y² and N(xy)^{-1} = N(x)^{-1}N(y)^{-1}.
Continuity: squaring and inversion are continuous on the topological groups of units, and N is continuous (norm-at-p).
acceptance: Pulling back (w, t) along ι gives w²·(t^{-1} ∘ N), not w²·(t ∘ N): with t trivial both agree, with w trivial they are inverse to each other.

sources.match: BHW define ρ through a group map T(ℤ_p) → T(ℤ_p) × ℤ_p^×; the printed map x ↦ (x², N(x)) is corrected to x ↦ (x², N(x)^{-1}) (E1).
(9.1) κ^{-1}(η)w(η²) = t∘N(η) holds for the inverted map.

nodes.title: The formula for ρ
nodes.statement: For w ∈ GeomWeight F p R, t : ℤ_p^× → R^× continuous and x ∈ 𝒪_p^×: ρ(ArithWeight.mk w t)(x) = w(x)²·t(N(x))^{-1}.
proofSteps: Unfold: ρ(mk w t)(x) = (mk w t)(ι x) = w(x²)·t(N(x)^{-1}) = w(x)²·t(N(x))^{-1}, using that w and t are homomorphisms.
acceptance: This is BHW's displayed κ = w²·(t^{-1} ∘ N_{F/ℚ}).
With the printed map x ↦ (x², N(x)) one would get w(x)²·t(N(x)) instead (E1).

nodes.title: ρ(w, t)·w^{-2} factors through the norm
nodes.statement: For κ = ρ(mk w t) and x ∈ 𝒪_p^×: κ(x)·w(x)^{-2} = t(N(x))^{-1}. In particular κ·w^{-2} factors through N : 𝒪_p^× → ℤ_p^×.
proofSteps: Rearrange weight-comparison-formula.
acceptance: BHW: 'κ(x)·w(x^{-2}) factors through some power of the norm'; here the factor is exactly t^{-1} ∘ N.
For (w, t) = (N^a, N^b) (algebraic), κ = N^{2a−b}.

sources.match: The factorisation through the norm.

nodes.title: ρ on totally positive global units
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real and η ∈ 𝒪_F^× totally positive (σ(η) > 0 for every real embedding σ). For κ = ρ(mk w t): κ(η)^{-1}·w(η)² = t(N(η)) = 1, where η is viewed in 𝒪_p^× by η ↦ 1 ⊗ η.
hypotheses: F totally real; η totally positive; R any topological commutative ring.
proofSteps: By weight-comparison-norm-factor, κ(η)^{-1}w(η)² = t(N(1 ⊗ η)).

N(1 ⊗ η) = N_{F/ℚ}(η) (norm-at-p) = ±1 since η is a unit (NumberField.isUnit_iff_norm), and N_{F/ℚ}(η) = ∏_σ σ(η) > 0 (Algebra.norm_eq_prod_embeddings, all embeddings real), so N_{F/ℚ}(η) = 1 and t(1) = 1.
acceptance: This is BHW (9.1), which makes the conditions (3) and (4) of §9 independent of representatives.
Total positivity is needed: for η = −1 and [F:ℚ] odd, t(N(η)) = t(−1), which can be −1.

uses.how: well-definedness of the arithmetic sheaves (3) and (4).

nodes.title: The radius parameter |T_κ|
nodes.statement: For a normed commutative ring A and κ ∈ GeomWeight F p A: |T_κ| := sup over x ∈ H_{r₀} = 1 + p^{r₀}𝒪_p of ‖κ(x) − 1‖, with r₀ = 1 for p odd and r₀ = 3 for p = 2. This is BHW's |T_κ| with the supremum restricted to a pro-p open subgroup, as AIP's coordinate T = κ(q) − 1 is; BHW print the supremum over all of 𝒪_p^× (source issue E2).
hypotheses: A a normed commutative ring; κ continuous.
proofSteps: Definition as an indexed supremum (iSup) over the subgroup principal-units H_{r₀}.
acceptance: The trivial character has |T_κ| = 0.
F = ℚ, p odd, κ = the Teichmüller character ω: |T_ω| = 0 (ω is trivial on 1 + pℤ_p), whereas BHW's printed supremum over ℤ_p^× gives 1.
F = ℚ, p odd, κ(x) = x^k: |T_κ| = |pk|_p.

uses.how: the radius of analytic continuation depends on |T_κ|.
|δ_κ| = max(|p|, |T_κ|) and ε_κ for the AIP comparison.

nodes.title: Continuous characters into uniform Banach algebras are bounded
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete normed ℚ_p-algebra whose norm is ultrametric and power-multiplicative (a uniform Banach algebra, such as an affinoid algebra with its spectral norm). Then every κ ∈ GeomWeight F p A has |T_κ| < 1.
hypotheses: A complete, ultrametric, ‖1‖ = 1, ‖·‖ power-multiplicative; κ continuous.
proofSteps: For x ∈ H_{r₀}, x^{p^n} → 1, so κ(x)^{p^n} → 1 by continuity.

If y = κ(x) − 1 had ‖y‖ ≥ 1, expand (1 + y)^{p^n} − 1 = y^{p^n} + Σ_{0<j<p^n} C(p^n, j) y^j. The first term has norm ‖y‖^{p^n} (power-multiplicativity), and each other term has norm ≤ |p|·‖y‖^j ≤ |p|·‖y‖^{p^n} < ‖y‖^{p^n}, since p divides C(p^n, j) and ‖y‖ ≥ 1. The norm is ultrametric, so ‖(1 + y)^{p^n} − 1‖ = ‖y‖^{p^n} ≥ 1 for all n, contradicting κ(x)^{p^n} → 1. Hence ‖κ(x) − 1‖ < 1.
x ↦ ‖κ(x) − 1‖ is continuous on the compact group H_{r₀} (open in the compact 𝒪_p^×), so its supremum is attained and is < 1.
acceptance: This is the coefficient-level form of 'an affinoid image is bounded'; unboundedness only occurs for non-affinoid families U, which need L0a's rigid spaces.
Power-multiplicativity is needed: for a non-uniform norm the binomial estimate fails.
The ultrametric hypothesis is needed for the domination step; archimedean normed algebras are excluded.

nodes.title: Analytic continuation of bounded weights
nodes.statement: Let κ be a bounded smooth weight κ : U → 𝒲*, i.e. a continuous character 𝒪_p^× → O^+(U)^× whose image lies in an affinoid of 𝒲*. Then there is r_κ > 0, depending only on p and |T_κ| (weight-radius-parameter) and hence uniform over U, such that for 0 < r ≤ r_κ the map κ : 𝒪_p^× × U → Ĝ_m extends uniquely to κ^an : B_r(𝒪_p^× : 1) × U → Ĝ_m, a morphism of adic groups in the first variable; equivalently, κ is analytic on every residue ball of radius r with values in O^+(U), in the sense of LocallyAnalyticDistributions L0.
hypotheses: κ bounded (image in an affinoid of 𝒲*); U smooth rigid over a perfectoid extension of L.

BHW print r_κ = |p|^{r₀}|T_κ| (Proposition 6.3), from AIP Proposition 2.8, which was not read. That value vanishes at the trivial weight, so it is recorded but not used; the theorem is stated with an existential radius, as in BHW's elliptic Proposition 3.12 and Definition 3.13.
proofSteps: Reduce to U affinoid, since a bounded U lies in an affinoid of 𝒲* (Definition 6.2).

If F is split in L, B_r(𝒪_p^× : 1) is the product over the embeddings of F into L of one-dimensional thickenings of the corresponding factors of 𝒪_p^×, and the elliptic argument applies coordinatewise: Buzzard, Eigenvarieties, Proposition 8.3, for affinoid U, with LocallyAnalyticDistributions L0 for a radius uniform over the compact group. In general pass to a finite Galois extension L'/L splitting F.
Descend along Gal(L'/L), which acts compatibly on the extensions by uniqueness.
Uniqueness: two analytic extensions agree on 𝒪_p^×, which meets every residue ball, so they agree on each ball by the identity theorem for power series on a ball.
acceptance: The restriction of κ^an to 𝒪_p^× × U is κ, and κ^an is multiplicative in the first variable (needed for the cocycle κ(cz + d) in O1–O2).
The radius depends only on |T_κ|, a supremum over the whole family, so one radius works on U.
The printed radius r_κ = |p|^{r₀}|T_κ| is 0 at the trivial weight, which is analytic everywhere; compare with AIP Proposition 2.8 before fixing ε^def_κ from it.
